transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: In an examination, a student scored \(72\%\) marks out of total \(450\) marks. How many marks did he obtain?
questions.keySolution:
Marks obtained = \(72\% \times 450\)
= \(\frac{72}{100} \times 450\)
= \(324\)

questions.stem: A student scored \(35\%\) marks and failed by \(25\) marks. If the passing marks are \(60\%\), what are the total marks?
questions.keySolution:
Let total marks be \(x\)
Student's marks = \(35\% \times x = 0.35x\)
Passing marks = \(60\% \times x = 0.6x\)
Difference = \(0.6x - 0.35x = 25\)
\(0.25x = 25\)
\(x = 100\)

questions.stem: In an exam, \(40\%\) students failed. If \(180\) students passed, what was the total number of students?
questions.keySolution:
If \(40\%\) failed, then \(60\%\) passed
Let total students be \(x\)
\(60\% \times x = 180\)
\(\frac{60}{100} \times x = 180\)
\(x = \frac{180 \times 100}{60} = 300\)

questions.stem: A student obtained \(456\) marks which is \(76\%\) of the total marks. Find the maximum marks.
questions.keySolution:
Let maximum marks be \(x\)
\(76\% \times x = 456\)
\(\frac{76}{100} \times x = 456\)
\(x = \frac{456 \times 100}{76} = 600\)

questions.stem: If \(25\%\) of the students in a class got first division, \(50\%\) got second division, and \(80\) students got third division, find the total number of students.
questions.keySolution:
First division = \(25\%\), Second division = \(50\%\)
Third division = \(100\% - 25\% - 50\% = 25\%\)
Let total students be \(x\)
\(25\% \times x = 80\)
\(\frac{25}{100} \times x = 80\)
\(x = \frac{80 \times 100}{25} = 320\)

questions.stem: In an examination, \(52\%\) of candidates failed in English, \(42\%\) failed in Mathematics. If \(17\%\) failed in both subjects and \(247\) passed in both, find total candidates.
questions.keySolution:
Failed in English = \(52\%\), Failed in Math = \(42\%\)
Failed in both = \(17\%\)
Failed in at least one = \(52\% + 42\% - 17\% = 77\%\)
Passed in both = \(100\% - 77\% = 23\%\)
Let total = \(x\), then \(23\% \times x = 247\)
\(x = \frac{247 \times 100}{23} = 1074.5\) (closest option)

questions.stem: A student's marks increased from \(360\) to \(450\). What is the percentage increase?
questions.keySolution:
Increase = \(450 - 360 = 90\)
Percentage increase = \(\frac{90}{360} \times 100\)
= \(\frac{90 \times 100}{360}\)
= \(25\%\)

questions.stem: In a test, a student scored \(80\%\) in the first attempt and \(90\%\) in the second attempt. If the maximum marks are \(500\), what is the increase in marks?
questions.keySolution:
First attempt marks = \(80\% \times 500 = 400\)
Second attempt marks = \(90\% \times 500 = 450\)
Increase = \(450 - 400 = 50\)

questions.stem: If the passing marks are \(33\%\) and a student got \(125\) marks out of \(500\), by how many marks did the student fail?
questions.keySolution:
Passing marks = \(33\% \times 500 = 165\)
Student's marks = \(125\)
Failed by = \(165 - 125 = 40\)

questions.stem: In an examination, \(70\%\) of students passed. If \(150\) students failed, how many students appeared for the exam?
questions.keySolution:
If \(70\%\) passed, then \(30\%\) failed
Let total students be \(x\)
\(30\% \times x = 150\)
\(\frac{30}{100} \times x = 150\)
\(x = \frac{150 \times 100}{30} = 500\)

questions.stem: A student scored \(78\%\) in Mathematics, \(85\%\) in Physics, and \(92\%\) in Chemistry. If each subject has \(100\) marks, what is his overall percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Total marks obtained = \(78 + 85 + 92 = 255\)
Total maximum marks = \(100 + 100 + 100 = 300\)
Overall percentage = \(\frac{255}{300} \times 100 = 85\%\)

questions.stem: In a class test, \(24\%\) students got A grade, \(36\%\) got B grade, and the remaining \(120\) students got C grade. Find the total number of students.
A student needs \(60\%\) marks to pass. He got \(200\) marks and passed by \(20\) marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.keySolution:
Passing marks = \(200 - 20 = 180\)
Let maximum marks be \(x\)
\(60\% \times x = 180\)
\(\frac{60}{100} \times x = 180\)
\(x = \frac{180 \times 100}{60} = 300\)

questions.stem: In an exam, \(45\%\) of total marks are required to pass. A student got \(40\%\) marks and failed by \(35\) marks. Find the total marks.
questions.keySolution:
Let total marks be \(x\)
Student's marks = \(40\% \times x = 0.4x\)
Passing marks = \(45\% \times x = 0.45x\)
Failed by \(35\) marks: \(0.45x - 0.4x = 35\)
\(0.05x = 35\)
\(x = \frac{35}{0.05} = 700\)

questions.stem: A student scored \(432\) marks out of \(600\). What percentage did he score?
In an examination, \(65\%\) candidates passed in English and \(70\%\) passed in Mathematics. If \(50\%\) passed in both subjects, what percentage failed in both?
questions.keySolution:
Passed in at least one = \(65\% + 70\% - 50\% = 85\%\)
Failed in both = \(100\% - 85\% = 15\%\)

questions.stem: A student got \(64\%\) in first term and \(76\%\) in second term. If the weightage is \(40\%\) and \(60\%\) respectively, find the overall percentage.
In a competitive exam, \(12\%\) candidates got selected. If \(264\) candidates got selected, how many appeared?
questions.keySolution:
Let total candidates be \(x\)
\(12\% \times x = 264\)
\(\frac{12}{100} \times x = 264\)
\(x = \frac{264 \times 100}{12} = 2200\)

questions.stem: A student's marks decreased from \(480\) to \(360\). Find the percentage decrease.
questions.keySolution:
Decrease = \(480 - 360 = 120\)
Percentage decrease = \(\frac{120}{480} \times 100\)
= \(\frac{120 \times 100}{480}\)
= \(25\%\)

questions.stem: In an exam with \(150\) questions, a student attempted \(80\%\) and got \(75\%\) of attempted questions correct. How many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.keySolution:
Questions attempted = \(80\% \times 150 = 120\)
Correct answers = \(75\% \times 120\)
= \(\frac{75}{100} \times 120 = 90\)

questions.stem: A student scored \(55\%\) in the first test and \(65\%\) in the second test. What is his average percentage?
If \(35\%\) of a number is \(280\), what is \(85\%\) of the same number?
In a school, \(42\%\) students are in science stream and \(38\%\) in commerce stream. If there are \(120\) students in arts stream, find the total students.
A student needs \(75\%\) marks to get distinction. He scored \(540\) marks and missed distinction by \(60\) marks. Find maximum marks.
questions.keySolution:
Distinction marks = \(540 + 60 = 600\)
Let maximum marks be \(x\)
\(75\% \times x = 600\)
\(\frac{75}{100} \times x = 600\)
\(x = \frac{600 \times 100}{75} = 800\)

questions.stem: In an exam, \(28\%\) students got A+, \(35\%\) got A, \(22\%\) got B+, and remaining \(90\) students got B or below. Find total students.
A student scored \(480\) marks out of \(600\) in first semester and \(420\) marks out of \(500\) in second semester. Which semester performance is better?
questions.keySolution:
First semester percentage = \(\frac{480}{600} \times 100 = 80\%\)
Second semester percentage = \(\frac{420}{500} \times 100 = 84\%\)
Second semester performance is better

questions.stem: In a test, \(20\%\) questions were very easy, \(50\%\) were easy, \(25\%\) were moderate, and remaining \(10\) questions were difficult. Find total questions.
questions.keySolution:
Very easy = \(20\%\), Easy = \(50\%\), Moderate = \(25\%\)
Difficult = \(100\% - 20\% - 50\% - 25\% = 5\%\)
Let total questions be \(x\)
\(5\% \times x = 10\)
\(x = \frac{10 \times 100}{5} = 200\)

questions.stem: A student got \(30\%\) in first subject, \(40\%\) in second subject, and \(50\%\) in third subject. If all subjects carry equal weightage, find overall percentage.
In an examination, a student scored \(85\%\) and got \(510\) marks. What were the maximum marks?
questions.keySolution:
Let maximum marks be \(x\)
\(85\% \times x = 510\)
\(\frac{85}{100} \times x = 510\)
\(x = \frac{510 \times 100}{85} = 600\)

questions.stem: A class has \(48\) students. If \(25\%\) are absent on a particular day, how many students are present?
questions.keySolution:
Absent students = \(25\% \times 48 = \frac{25}{100} \times 48 = 12\)
Present students = \(48 - 12 = 36\)

questions.stem: In a test of \(200\) marks, a student loses \(2\) marks for each wrong answer. If he attempted \(90\) questions correctly out of \(100\), what is his score percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Correct answers = \(90\), Wrong answers = \(10\)
Marks gained = \(90 \times 2 = 180\)
Marks lost = \(10 \times 2 = 20\)
Net score = \(180 - 20 = 160\)
Percentage = \(\frac{160}{200} \times 100 = 80\%\)

questions.stem: A student got \(72\) marks in English, \(84\) marks in Mathematics and \(90\) marks in Science. If the passing percentage is \(60\%\) and each subject is of \(100\) marks, did he pass overall?
questions.keySolution:
Total marks obtained = \(72 + 84 + 90 = 246\)
Total maximum marks = \(100 + 100 + 100 = 300\)
Percentage = \(\frac{246}{300} \times 100 = 82\%\)
Since \(82\% > 60\%\), he passed

questions.stem: In a competitive exam, the cut-off is \(150\) marks out of \(250\). What is the cut-off percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cut-off percentage = \(\frac{150}{250} \times 100\)
= \(\frac{150 \times 100}{250}\)
= \(60\%\)

questions.stem: A student's rank improved from \(85\) to \(68\) in a class of \(200\) students. What is the percentage improvement in rank?
questions.keySolution:
Improvement in rank = \(85 - 68 = 17\)
Percentage improvement = \(\frac{17}{85} \times 100\)
= \(\frac{17 \times 100}{85} = 20\%\)

questions.stem: In an exam, \(15\%\) students got distinction, \(25\%\) got first class, \(35\%\) got second class, \(20\%\) got third class, and remaining \(20\) students failed. Find total students.
questions.keySolution:
Passed students = \(15\% + 25\% + 35\% + 20\% = 95\%\)
Failed students = \(100\% - 95\% = 5\%\)
Let total students be \(x\)
\(5\% \times x = 20\)
\(x = \frac{20 \times 100}{5} = 400\)

questions.stem: A student scored \(76\%\) in first year, \(82\%\) in second year, and \(88\%\) in third year. Find his average percentage over three years.

In a test, negative marking is \(\frac{1}{4}\) mark for each wrong answer. A student attempted \(80\) questions out of \(100\), got \(60\) correct. If each correct answer carries \(1\) mark, what is his score?
questions.keySolution:
Correct answers = \(60\), Wrong answers = \(80 - 60 = 20\)
Marks gained = \(60 \times 1 = 60\)
Marks deducted = \(20 \times \frac{1}{4} = 5\)
Net score = \(60 - 5 = 55\)

questions.stem: A student needs \(40\%\) to pass in each subject. He got \(35\%\) in Math, \(45\%\) in Physics, and \(38\%\) in Chemistry. In how many subjects did he fail?
questions.keySolution:
Passing percentage = \(40\%\)
Math: \(35\% < 40\%\) (Failed)
Physics: \(45\% > 40\%\) (Passed)
Chemistry: \(38\% < 40\%\) (Failed)
Failed in \(2\) subjects

questions.stem: In a class of \(150\) students, \(60\%\) are boys. How many girls are there in the class?
A student scored \(456\) marks and his percentile rank is \(85\)th. This means \(85\%\) students scored less than him. If \(1200\) students appeared, how many scored more than him?
questions.keySolution:
Students who scored less = \(85\% \times 1200 = 1020\)
Students who scored more = \(1200 - 1020 = 180\)
(Note: The student himself is not counted in either category)

questions.stem: In a scholarship exam, top \(5\%\) students get the scholarship. If \(2400\) students appeared and \(540\) marks is the cut-off, what percentage of maximum marks is the cut-off?
questions.keySolution:
We know the cut-off marks (\(540\)) and number of students (\(2400\))
But maximum marks are not given
We cannot determine the percentage without knowing maximum marks

questions.stem: A student got \(80\%\) in theory and \(90\%\) in practical. If theory carries \(70\%\) weightage and practical \(30\%\) weightage, find his overall percentage.

In a multiple choice test of \(60\) questions, \(4\) marks are given for correct answer and \(1\) mark is deducted for wrong answer. A student attempted all questions and scored \(200\) marks. How many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.keySolution:
Let correct answers = \(x\), wrong answers = \(60-x\)
Total score = \(4x - (60-x) = 200\)
\(4x - 60 + x = 200\)
\(5x = 260\)
\(x = 52\)

questions.stem: A student's aggregate percentage in \(5\) subjects is \(76\%\). If he scored \(85\%, 72\%, 80\%, 68\%\) in first four subjects, what is his percentage in the fifth subject?
questions.keySolution:
Total percentage for \(5\) subjects = \(76\% \times 5 = 380\%\)
First four subjects total = \(85\% + 72\% + 80\% + 68\% = 305\%\)
Fifth subject percentage = \(380\% - 305\% = 75\%\)

questions.stem: In an entrance exam, a candidate needs \(50\%\) marks to qualify. The exam has \(200\) questions of \(1\) mark each with negative marking of \(0.25\) for wrong answers. If a student attempted \(160\) questions and got \(120\) correct, did he qualify?
questions.keySolution:
Correct = \(120\), Wrong = \(160-120 = 40\)
Marks = \(120 \times 1 - 40 \times 0.25 = 120 - 10 = 110\)
Percentage = \(\frac{110}{200} \times 100 = 55\%\)
Since \(55\% > 50\%\), he qualified

questions.stem: A class teacher announced that students securing more than \(85\%\) will get a prize. Out of \(40\) students, \(8\) got the prize. What percentage of students got the prize?
questions.keySolution:
Percentage of students who got prize = \(\frac{8}{40} \times 100\)
= \(\frac{8 \times 100}{40}\)
= \(20\%\)

questions.stem: A student appeared for \(4\) tests. His scores were \(85\%, 78\%, 92\%\) and \(81\%\). What is his average score?

In a college, \(45\%\) students study Science, \(35\%\) study Commerce, and \(320\) students study Arts. If some students study multiple streams, what is the minimum number of students in the college?
questions.keySolution:
Arts students = \(320\)
If only Arts students don't overlap with others:
Arts = \(100\% - 45\% - 35\% = 20\%\) (minimum case)
Let total students = \(x\)
\(20\% \times x = 320\)
\(x = \frac{320 \times 100}{20} = 1600\)
